articles.title: The Liberation review – Carrie Coon joins all-female cult in unsettling drama
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: Director Guy Nattiv draws on personal experience for an 80s-set tale of a woman abandoning her family for a creepy commune. We remain fascinated and horrified by the hows and whys of cult narratives, how someone could be so seduced by something so unknown and why they would…
body: His attempt to try to understand who she was and why she acted in such a way has led to unsettling drama The Liberation, a fictionalised tale that acts as a form of therapy for him and a mostly successful antidote to more sensationalist cult stories for us. Enough Netflix docuseries and schlocky horror movies have given us a more extreme and often violent idea of how cults infect and destroy vulnerable people but Nattiv opts for a more thoughtful slow-burn. He’s recruited a suitably thoughtful actor in Carrie Coon, no stranger to this particular psychology having broken out in The Leftovers, one of the more intelligent cult dramas in recent years.

It’s a rare big-screen lead for Coon, an actor who broke out a little later than most, and she tears into it, working hard to try and bring us into the mindset of someone who would do something so unimaginable. We might never truly understand or even like her all that much but we believe her and like Nattiv, we’re haunted by her actions.

articles.title: Resident Evil review – Zach Cregger’s rebooted action horror is a wild rollercoaster ride
articles.summary: The Weapons director delivers a seat-edge thriller with a standout lead performance from Austin Abrams as an everyman navigating chaos. Typically horror fans react to blatant on-screen stupidity with vocal derision. Don’t go in there! Girl, get out of the house! Guys, ignore that distress signal!
body: Bryan is a courier – a glorified Postmates driver, in his own estimation – who postpones the end of his shift to take one last night-time run, driving an important item from one hospital to another in a snowstorm without the proper tires or four-wheel drive. After all, the distance and urgency means double pay. When he hits a mysterious woman who emerges suddenly on to a slick road, he’s drawn into a hellish outbreak that will look familiar to fans of the Resident Evil video game series (or maybe the previous six-movie Milla Jovovich franchise, which apparently drifted afield from the games’ storylines).

articles.title: Smile at Last review – photo-love-story style parable of a teen abandoned at a tough Soviet youth facility
articles.summary: With handheld camerawork, this unsentimental rite of passage film follows Mari, who tries to escape from a residential home in Estonia. This intriguing 1985 film from Estonia uses nonprofessionals and handheld camerawork, which brings faces looming up to the screen.
body: It is at one level a kind of coming-of-age story, but entirely without that genre’s usual, sentimental sense of something finally learned or gained from an emotional rite of passage – something finally to smile about, in fact. Actually, it is more of a mysterious parable, couched in the language of soap opera or photo-love story, depicting the Soviet state and its gruesome pretension to be caring or nurturing.

There is a dreamlike quality to the action, despite its ostensible kitchen-sink realism. It is almost a kind of pastoral: the young people in this institution apparently have no school lessons, they seem free to just drift around, playing games, pursuing crushes, quarrels and intrigues, until it all turns sour. But there is a curious kind of acceptance; has Mari become institutionalised, just as the head teacher predicted, when she brought Mari back from the police station? A strange, bittersweet vignette.
points: With handheld camerawork, this unsentimental rite of passage film follows Mari, who tries to escape from a residential home in Estonia.

articles.title: Guy Pearce Reunites With Andrew Baird for Irish Thriller ‘Bottle’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Guy Pearce and filmmaker Andrew Baird will reunite for their fourth film, an upcoming Irish thriller titled “Bottle.” The actor will play Jimmy, a historically violent pub owner who traps a troubled young man named Cillian after he breaks into his bar in search of a pint.
body: “‘Bottle’ brought to mind the classic crime films of the ‘70s, such as Peter Yates’ ‘The Friends of Eddie Coyle,’ with a similar DNA to John Hillcoat’s ‘The Proposition,’ which Guy starred in,” Baird said. “What separates this from my previous pictures is that it is inherently Irish and lives in a very dark, traumatic and bruised world, reflecting an old Ireland that I know very well and grew up in. It has never been captured in this way before on film.”

Pearce previously collaborated with Baird on “Zone 414,” “Sunrise” and “The Marshal,” which is set to release in 2027. The actor most recently starred in Ridley Scott’s “The Dog Stars” alongside Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley and Josh Brolin. The film brought in $8 million domestically during its opening weekend despite costing over $80 million to produce.
Pearce is repped by Independent Talent Group and Creative Artists Agency. Baird is repped by Source Management + Production.

articles.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
articles.summary: Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile. Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The…
body: Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

Born in Chile in 1941, Guzmán initially worked in advertising before studying film, first in Chile and then in Madrid. On his return to Chile, Guzmán responded to the febrile political atmosphere after Allende’s election in 1970, eventually completing the mammoth Battle of Chile documentary that chronicled Pinochet’s ultimately successful attempt to overthrow Allende, resulting in the latter’s suicide. Guzmán did not shrink from the brutality of the period, even including footage shot by camera operator Leonardo Henrichsen as he is shot dead by the soldier he is filming.
points: Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile.

articles.title: How American High Scored Big With ‘Minimum Wage’ Netflix Series While Building a Pipeline for the Next Generation of Comedians (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: It all started with Jeremy Garelick’s simple but ambitious plan for American High: Buy a high school in upstate New York and turn it into the hottest filming spot in town for coming-of-age comedies.
body: “It’s the same philosophy we have with film, but in the digital space. If someone’s doing something cool, we’ll just amplify it without all the gatekeeping,” American High president Will Phelps says. “It’s the model that other people were too afraid to do. And now turn the page, everyone wants to give those creators $10 million to make the next ‘Obsession.’ I think we were probably just there five years earlier.”

“Unlike all the studios and giant companies that like to just be reactive and see what’s working, they don’t want to take chances on first-time directors or actors,” Garelick adds, with a majority of American High’s films being helmed by first-time directors (including Jillian Bell and Jason Orley).

Working with Netflix was a natural fit for Garelick, who directed the 2023 Adam Sandler movie “Murder Mystery 2” and the show “Best Worst Weekend Ever” for the streamer. “This is the biggest opportunity we’ve had at American High in terms of getting our stuff to the broadest audience,” he says.

articles.title: Ex-BBC presenter questions role of Royal Family in new documentary
articles.summary: John Humphrys, who presented Today and the Nine O'Clock News, heads a new Channel 4 documentary on the topic.
body: Veteran broadcaster John Humphrys has said the people of the United Kingdom should "be able to choose our leaders" as he releases a documentary exploring the role of the Royal Family.
Humphrys, who for decades was one of the most prominent faces on the BBC, is presenting a new Channel 4 documentary called The Royals: Time to Go?
Speaking to BBC Radio Wales Breakfast, the Cardiff-born presenter said he "admires" King Charles III in many ways, but said it was a "matter of choice".
In the documentary, Humphrys speaks to both critics and supporters of the monarchy, and makes the case for electing a president as the head of state.

articles.title: Legendary Nigerian actor Olu Jacobs dies aged 84
articles.summary: Olu Jacobs was one of Nigeria's most recognised actors, whose career spanned several decades.
body: His wife, veteran actress Joke Silva, announced his death and asked for privacy while the family mourns.
Silva announced his passing in a statement describing the celebrated actor as "The Lion of Lufodo" and saying his life was "well lived and fought".
Some of his notable films include My Kingdom, Covert Operation and One Fine Day.
He was regarded as one of the father figures of Nollywood, as Nigeria's film industry in known, commanding widespread respect and admiration across the country.

articles.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Adds Brendan Morgan, David Tomlinson and More to Season 2
articles.summary: The second season of Crave-HBO Max's hit series has announced six additions to the cast including for the roles of Zane Boodram and a newly renamed Cody Kent.
body: Heated Rivalry has added six more actors to its upcoming second season.

Brendan Morgan ( F*** Marry Kill, The Handmaid’s Tale ) joins as Zane Boodram, a professional hockey player on Ottawa’s team. David Tomlinson ( Fellow Travelers ) will play Cody Kent, a player on the Toronto team. The role is confirmed to be the newly renamed Dallas Kent character from Rachel Reid’s novels.

Lauren Chan ( The Devil Wears Prada 2 ) will play Gen, an employee of the Ottawa team that works alongside new season two lead Harris Drover ( Justice Smith ). Nick Stahl ( Let the Right One In ) joins as Curtis Barrett, father to new season two lead Troy Barrett, played by Charlie Gillespie.
